plan.topic: Does semaglutide reduce muscle strength? The Diabetes, Obesity and Metabolism meta-analysis of handgrip strength (19 Oct 2026)
plan.angle: Title: 'Does Semaglutide Weaken Grip Strength? What Studies Show'. Answer within 10 s: across 10 pooled studies (660 people on semaglutide), average handgrip strength showed no clear change, but the researchers rate the evidence as very low certainty and the studies varied a lot. One line: lean mass (weight) is not the same as strength (function). Separate anchor: in the SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy (tirzepatide; adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes; 72 weeks), about a quarter of the weight lost was lean mass. Recommended habits, not proven on the drug: a protein food at each meal unless your clinician has told you to limit protein (for example, kidney disease), and muscle-strengthening activity at least 2 days a week, starting gently. One GI line, 'don't stop or change your medicines on your own', the full prescriber line, and the CTA only if the named long-form is live.

plan.why: Muscle outcome questions are proven for us (101 and 131 views). The handgrip-strength result is a fact we haven't published, and the Short funnels to the already-live strength-training long-form. | fact-check: The meta-analysis exists (summarised at https://www.omnicuris.com/medshots/daily_updates/semaglutide-muscle-strength-systematic-review-meta-analysis_20-Oct-26_14-18). 16 reports from 11 unique investigations. 10 studies with 660 semaglutide-treated participants were pooled. Pooled handgrip change −0.16 kgf (95% CI −1.98 to 1.65), not statistically significant. I² was 90.8% with a wide prediction interval, and the authors rate the certainty of the evidence as very low. 'Strength mostly held up' goes further than the paper. Say 'no clear average change, but the evidence is very low certainty and the studies varied a lot'. The change was absolute (kgf). Confirm whether it was also reported relative to body weight, and confirm the journal and online date (the angle says 19 Oct 2026; the summary is dated 20 Oct) on the journal page before scripting. The working title says 'Losing Muscle', but the study measured strength, not muscle mass, so the title has to say strength. SURMOUNT-1 anchor: say 'lean mass', not 'muscle', and label it as a separate tirzepatide trial. Confirm the strength-training long-form is published before naming it in the CTA.

social.instagram_caption:
Semaglutide and handgrip strength: a new meta-analysis found no clear average change, but very low certainty evidence.

A new meta-analysis pooled 10 studies and 660 people taking semaglutide — and found no clear average change in handgrip strength.

But here's the catch: most studies compared people before and after with no placebo group, results varied a lot between studies, and researchers rated the evidence very low certainty.

Also worth knowing: lean mass isn't the same as strength. Separately, body scans from tirzepatide's SURMOUNT-1 trial (adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes) showed about a quarter of weight lost over 72 weeks was lean mass, all doses combined — similar to the share in the placebo group, which lost less weight overall.

Habits worth discussing with your clinician (not proven on these medicines): protein at each meal — unless your clinician limits it, like for kidney disease — and muscle-strengthening activity on 2 days a week, per CDC guidance. Start gently.

Common semaglutide side effects include nausea and diarrhea. Don't stop or change your medicines on your own.

Save this for your next doctor visit.

factcheck.summary:
I checked every factual claim against its source and they hold up. The meta-analysis numbers (s1) are right: 10 pooled studies, 660 adults on semaglutide, a pooled handgrip change of −0.16 kgf (95% CI −1.98 to 1.65), I² of 90.8%, very low certainty under GRADE, and mostly uncontrolled before-vs-after data. The tirzepatide numbers (s2, the SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy) are right too: 124 people on tirzepatide (all doses combined) versus 36 on placebo, over 72 weeks, with 26% versus 25% of weight lost as lean mass. "About a quarter in both groups" is a fair summary. The population is described correctly, and the Short labels this as a different drug in a different trial.

The CDC strength guideline (s3, last reviewed 20 Dec 2023) and the semaglutide side effects from MedlinePlus (s4, revised 15 May 2026) also check out. The framing is careful. It says "no clear average change", not "no effect". It names the missing placebo groups and the very low certainty. It keeps lean mass and strength separate. It flags the protein habit as not proven on these drugs and adds a kidney-disease caveat. It carries the full prescriber line and "Not personal advice", and the hook pays off within 10 s.

I'd fix four small wording points:
1. The CDC says "at least" 2 days, so "on two days a week" narrows it.
2. S2-7 covers semaglutide side effects but not those of tirzepatide, which S2-5 brings in.
3. The narration runs about 183 words, against the 170-word target.
4. s1 is a secondary summary, because I couldn't find the primary paper online.

issues.claim: Plus muscle-strengthening on two days a week, as the CDC recommends.
issues.problem: The CDC says adults need muscle-strengthening activity on at least 2 days a week, working all major muscle groups. Saying "on two days" turns a minimum into a fixed amount.
issues.fix: Narration: "Plus muscle-strengthening on at least two days a week, as the CDC recommends. Our tip: start gently." On-screen text: "2+ strength days a week". Stat label: "days a week of muscle-strengthening, at least (CDC)".

issues.claim: Common semaglutide side effects: nausea and diarrhea.
issues.problem: S2-5 brings in tirzepatide, but the safety beat only gives semaglutide's side effects. Our house rule is to state common side effects for each named drug.
issues.fix: Narration: "Common side effects of both drugs: nausea and diarrhea. Don't stop or change your medicines on your own. Not personal advice: talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you." List item: "Common (both drugs): nausea, diarrhea". If you keep this line, add the tirzepatide MedlinePlus page (https://medlineplus.gov/druginfo/meds/a622044.html) as a source.

issues.problem: The narration is about 183 words, over the 170-word Short target. It's still well within the 178 s limit.
issues.fix: S2-3: change to "But here's the catch: most studies had no placebo group, and results varied a lot. Researchers rate the evidence very low certainty." S2-5: cut "which lost less weight" so the line ends "That's similar to the placebo group." Together these save about 13 words.

issues.claim: 660 people on semaglutide across 10 pooled studies
issues.problem: The muted-viewer rule asks each stat card to name the population and the measure. The card doesn't say these are adults, or that the figure compares the same people before and after.
issues.fix: Stat label: "adults on semaglutide, 10 pooled before-vs-after studies".

issues.claim: MedShots summary of Machado LG et al., Diabetes Obes Metab 2026

issues.fix: Keep s1 for now. Swap in the canonical Diabetes Obes Metab or PubMed URL for Machado LG et al. 2026 once it's indexed.

audio.soundNotes: Base music sits a touch hot in pauses (-12.3 dB vs ~-14 target) while under-voice is already in range, so pulled the bed down ~1.5 dB overall (0.84×) rather than altering per-cue music balance. Thinned three over-dense SFX clusters (the stat reveal at ~3.2s, the transition at ~11.8s, the side-effect chips at ~55.5s and ~65.9s) to 3-4 hits max per second, and pulled down three cues around the "chips" reveal (22, 26, 27) that measured far louder than the voice (-4.5 to -10 dB) along with dropping a redundant tick. Left the quiet swell at 17.9s and the pause-level transition swells/whooshes alone since they're already within the −6 to −12 dB pause/transition window. Added two bespoke sounds for story beats the stock kit can't cover: a tactile grip-squeeze under the handgrip-strength reveal and a calm resolving pad under the final "no clear average change" takeaway.
